messages:
maria-cs: FYI escalation from Acme — rerank endpoint returns 422 and sometimes all-zero scores for same payload. Customer pasted a minimal repro. They also rotated API keys earlier today so they asked if auth could be related. :eyes:
eli-eng: can you paste the exact payload + the 422 body? also which model/version and endpoint params (collection, k, rerank_level)?
maria-cs: here's the stripped repro they sent (redacted ids):
```
POST /v1/rerank
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
{
  "model":"redwood/rerank-v1",
  "query":"how to reset password",
  "documents": [
    { "id":"d1", "text":"...", "query":"user intent: reset" },
    { "id":"d2", "text":"...", "query":"user intent: reset" }
  ],
  "candidates": [
    "d1", "d2"
  ]
}
```
maria-cs: Response they get: 422 Unprocessable Entity + body: `{"error":"invalid input: unrecognized field \"query\" in document object"}`; sometimes a 200 with all scores 0.0 when they remove the top-level `query` but keep per-doc `query` fields.
ben-ml: interesting. They used both `documents` array (objects) and `candidates` array (ids). Two things stand out: 1) per-document field named `query` collides with top-level `query` concept in our validation, 2) mixed array element types in `candidates` (string ids) vs expecting objects can trigger different parsing paths.
eli-eng: I can repro locally. If `candidates` contains strings we take a fast path and expand by id lookup; if docs carry a `query` key our JSON schema validation treats it as an unexpected property -> 422. The all-zero scores case likely comes from the fast path failing to align candidate->document mapping when there are duplicate ids or mixed types.
maria-cs: Customer says they used a generator that injects a `query` field into each doc metadata for internal QA. They thought nested keys were fine because it was only metadata.
ben-ml: Root cause seems to be twofold: schema strictness + confusing error message. We should either accept `query` inside document objects (map under `metadata`) or throw clearer error pointing them to rename fields. Also we need to normalize `candidates` element types.
eli-eng: Quick repro steps for eng: 1) run above curl with both top-level `query` and per-doc `query` -> 422, 2) change `candidates` to objects [{"id":"d1"},...] -> sometimes returns 200 with 0.0 scores, 3) remove per-doc `query` -> OK.
maria-cs: I suggested a workaround to customer: rename per-doc field to `metadata.query_text` or `doc_query`, or send `candidates` as objects. They tried `metadata.query_text` and it worked. Customer accepted workaround but wants root cause fixed.
oncall-bot: Ticket created TKT-4321: "Rerank input validation - nested `query` field and mixed candidates types cause 422/zero-scores" assigned to eng-oncall.
eli-eng: assigning to me. I'll add a more descriptive validation error if docs contain `query` and ensure candidates string/object handling is consistent. I'll also add unit tests for mixed-type arrays. ETA EOD. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ben-ml: also log a regression test where per-doc metadata keys like `query` are preserved (we should probably namespace metadata during ingestion).
maria-cs: I'll follow up with the customer with the workaround and tell them we have a fix in progress. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
